title: Time Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Time Calculator: Add or subtract hours, minutes and seconds. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Time Calculator](/time-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Add or subtract hours, minutes and seconds. Enter your time 1 — hours, time 1 — minutes, operation, time 2 — hours and time 2 — minutes and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Add or subtract durations in hours and minutes without the base-60 headaches. Also shows decimal hours for timesheets and payroll. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Date & Time tools include [Age Calculator](/age-calculator), [Days Between Dates Calculator](/days-between-dates-calculator) and [Date Calculator](/date-calculator). People also look for this tool as "hours calculator", "add time calculator", "time duration calculator".

## How to use the Time Calculator

Start by entering your time 1 — hours, then entering your time 1 — minutes, choosing your operation from the list, entering your time 2 — hours and finally entering your time 2 — minutes. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your time 1 — hours.
2. Enter your time 1 — minutes.
3. Choose your operation from the list.
4. Enter your time 2 — hours.
5. Enter your time 2 — minutes.
6. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.

## Formula

Convert each time to minutes, add or subtract, then convert back: hours = ⌊min ÷ 60⌋, minutes = min mod 60.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Time Calculator](/time-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 2h 45m + 1h 30m = 4h 15m = 255 minutes = 4.25 decimal hours. Try the same figures in the [Time Calculator](/time-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Time 1 — hours: 2, Time 1 — minutes: 45, Operation: Add, Time 2 — hours: 1, Time 2 — minutes: 30), the [Time Calculator](/time-calculator) returns Result: 4h 15m, Total minutes: 255, Decimal hours: 4.25. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Age Calculator](/age-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Decimal hours × hourly rate = pay.
- 15 minutes = 0.25 h, 30 = 0.5 h, 45 = 0.75 h.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I convert minutes to decimal hours?

Divide minutes by 60. 20 minutes = 0.333 hours. Try it with your own numbers in the [Time Calculator](/time-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I get a negative result?

Yes, when subtracting a longer duration from a shorter one. Try it with your own numbers in the [Time Calculator](/time-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Time Calculator use?

Convert each time to minutes, add or subtract, then convert back: hours = ⌊min ÷ 60⌋, minutes = min mod 60. You can see it in action in the [Time Calculator](/time-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Time Calculator?

Just Time 1 — hours, Time 1 — minutes, Operation, Time 2 — hours and Time 2 — minutes. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
